observations: Truck-mounted drilling rig: orange mast/derrick structure bolted onto the rear bed of a white cab-over truck.
Grille badge reads 'NISSAN DIESEL' in photo 0 and 2; a partial orange 'R' logo is visible on the mast in photo 1 but no full drill-rig brand/model is legible.
Windscreen and cab are heavily dust-covered; body panels show rust streaks and faded orange paint.
Hydraulic hoses on the mast (photo 1) look worn, kinked and rust-stained.
Tyres show visible wear and the vehicle is parked on bare earth, not in an active drilling pose.
No people, no engine running, no drilling-in-progress, no close-up of hour-meter, engine bay, or rig data plate in any photo.
Hand-written stickers on windscreen ('Best Parts Steering', 'No Hand Signal') are informal, not manufacturer markings.
License plate is partially visible but not fully legible for verification.

identity.kind: truck-mounted borehole/water-well drilling rig on a Nissan Diesel (UD) cab-over truck chassis
identity.brand: Nissan Diesel (truck chassis only, rig manufacturer unreadable)

claims.evidence: No photo or clip shows the engine running, the mast operating, or drilling in progress; truck looks dusty and idle.
No service receipt, invoice, or fresh-parts photo provided; visible rust and grime suggest the opposite but this is not conclusive.
Drill rods, bits, mud pump, and other ancillary tools are not shown in any photo; only the mast and truck body are visible.
No data plate, serial number, or manufacturer nameplate is legible in any photo.

risks.risk: Engine and drivetrain may not start or run (truck and rig share or depend on engine power).
risks.proof: Video of engine starting, idling, and the rig's drive/power-takeoff engaging.
risks.if_unproven: priced as not working / needing engine repair

risks.risk: Hydraulic system (hoses, pump, cylinders) may be leaking or failing, as hoses appear worn and rust-stained.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of hydraulic pump, hose fittings, and a clip of the mast raising/lowering under pressure.

risks.risk: Mast/derrick structural rust or cracks hidden under paint could compromise safe drilling load.
risks.proof: Close-up shots of weld joints and mast base, plus any structural inspection certificate.
risks.if_unproven: priced as structurally unverified, discounted for rust risk

risks.risk: Missing ancillary equipment (drill rods, bits, mud pump, compressor) needed for 'all parts complete' claim.
risks.proof: Photos of the full tool/parts inventory laid out.

risks.risk: Vehicle roadworthiness (tyres, brakes, registration/insurance) unknown; tyres look worn.
risks.proof: Clear photo of tyre tread, brake pads, and current vehicle particulars/registration papers.
risks.if_unproven: priced as needing tyre/brake replacement and unregistered

risks.risk: Ownership/title fraud risk — no proof of seller's right to sell a heavy commercial rig.
risks.proof: Photo of vehicle registration/ownership documents matching seller's name.
risks.if_unproven: treated as unverified ownership, added caution but not automatic fraud flag

proof_requests: Video of the engine starting and the drill mast raising/lowering or drilling.
Close-up of the rig's data/serial plate and the truck's chassis number.
Photos of included tools: drill rods, bits, mud pump, compressor.
Close-up of tyres, brakes, and hydraulic hose fittings.
response.reason: The item is clearly identifiable as a truck-mounted borehole drilling rig on a Nissan Diesel chassis, but every seller claim of good working condition and completeness is unproven and the visible rust, dust, and worn hoses point to a long-idle, unmaintained unit, so it must be priced at its worst-case (non-functional, needs servicing) condition.
